# React Flow parity — measured

**Generated by `npm run rangerflow:parity`. Do not edit by hand.**

A scorecard we wrote from imagination would only measure our imagination.
So the reference answers in the geometry tables below are not written down —
they are computed by React Flow itself. `harness/oracles/reactflow_oracle.mjs`
calls `getBezierPath`, `getSmoothStepPath`, `getStraightPath`,
`getViewportForBounds`, `pointToRendererPoint` and `getNodesBounds` out of
`@xyflow/system` — the package React Flow is built on, the same functions a
React Flow app calls — and RangerFlow is asked the same questions in
`tests/ParityDump.rgr`.

Edge paths are compared by **resampling both curves by arc length**, not by
string equality: what matters is whether the line goes through the same
places, not whether it was written with the same commands.

| Family | Reference | Score | Worst |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| Edge geometry | `getBezierPath, getStraightPath, getSmoothStepPath` | 320/320 — 100% | 0.002 px |
| Viewport algebra | `pointToRendererPoint, rendererPointToPoint` | 32/32 — 100% | 0.000 px |
| fitView | `getViewportForBounds` | 36/36 — 100% | 0.000 px |
| Node bounds | `getNodesBounds` | 2/2 — 100% | 0.000 px |
| Selection overlap | `getRectsOverlappingArea` | 5/5 — 100% | 0.438 px |
| Force layout | `d3-force` | 5/5 — 100% | 0.065 % shape |
| Behaviour | `probes against FlowEditor` | 45/51 — 88% | — |
| **Overall** | mean of the 7 families | **98.3%** | |

The overall figure is the mean of the family percentages, not of the cases:
320 edge paths and 50 capabilities are not 370 equally important facts, and a
score that said so would move whenever a case was added.

## Geometry

`exact` ≤ 0.001 px · `match` ≤ 0.5 px · `close` ≤ 5 px · `differs` beyond that.

| Family | React Flow function | Cases | exact | match | close | differs | Worst |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Edge geometry | `getBezierPath, getStraightPath, getSmoothStepPath` | 320 | 313 | 7 | 0 | 0 | 0.002 px |
| Viewport algebra | `pointToRendererPoint, rendererPointToPoint` | 32 | 32 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0.000 px |
| fitView | `getViewportForBounds` | 36 | 36 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0.000 px |
| Node bounds | `getNodesBounds` | 2 | 2 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0.000 px |
| Selection overlap | `getRectsOverlappingArea` | 5 | 4 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0.438 px |

## Force layout against d3-force

The same 30-node graph, the same four forces in the same order, the same
parameters, ticked by hand. `max` and `rms` are how far a node ended up from
where d3 put it. **Shape error** compares every pairwise distance instead,
normalised by the reference layout's own scale — two runs that differ by a
rotation or a translation are the same layout, and that is the number worth
reading.

| Tick | Max deviation | RMS | Shape error |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 0 | 0.000 px | 0.000 px | 0.00% |
| 1 | 0.010 px | 0.008 px | 0.00% |
| 10 | 0.381 px | 0.075 px | 0.01% |
| 50 | 0.315 px | 0.125 px | 0.02% |
| 300 | 1.414 px | 0.480 px | 0.06% |

## Behaviour

Every row is a capability **React Flow documents for itself** — a prop, a
component, or an example it ships. `done` requires a named probe in
`tests/ParityDump.rgr` that drove the real `FlowEditor` through
`pointerDown` / `pointerMove` / `pointerUp` and passed. A row with no probe is
`todo` however finished it feels, and a probe that fails turns the row red —
which is worse than `todo`, because it means the documentation lies.

## Deliberate divergences

Known, understood, and not going to be fixed — listed because "we decided to
differ" and "we never noticed" look identical in a table of numbers.

- **5 geometry cases** — React Flow rounds the overlap area UP (`Math.ceil`). RangerFlow keeps the true area. Only the sign of the number decides whether a node is selected, and both agree on that, so the rounding is not reproduced.
- **the force layout** — d3 gives each force its own seeded generator; RangerFlow has one. The jiggle only fires on exactly-coincident points and is 1e-6 wide, which is the residue left at tick 300.

## What this does not measure

- **Pixels.** RangerFlow draws through EVG and React Flow through the DOM;
  comparing rendered images would measure font hinting, not parity.
- **Anything with no probe.** A `todo` row means nobody has proved it, not
  that it is known to be absent — though for the rows above, it is.
- **React Flow's React-ness.** Hooks, controlled state, SSR and the component
  API are outside what a non-React library can be scored against.
